title: Algorithms and Small Functions
summary: An algorithm is a set of steps for a job. C++ has ready-made steps for sorting and counting. A lambda is a small function written where you need it.
introduction: An algorithm is a set of steps for a job. C++ has ready-made steps for sorting and counting. A lambda is a small function written where you need it. Read one example at a time. Save it in a .cpp file and use the compiler from the setup lesson to run it.
learningObjectives: Sort a list from smallest to largest
Count values that fit a rule
Write a small function with a lambda

blocks.text: std::sort puts values in order. begin() points to the first item. end() marks the place just after the last item.

blocks.title: algorithms-lambdas.cpp

blocks.text: Count values that fit a rule
The lambda [](int n) { return n > 5; } answers yes or no for each number. count_if counts the yes answers.

blocks.title: algorithms-lambdas.cpp

blocks.text: Use a value from nearby code
The name in [limit] lets the lambda use a copy of limit. This is called a capture. It is like putting a note inside the small function.

blocks.title: algorithms-lambdas.cpp
Watch out
blocks.text: Do not guess which values a lambda can use. Put names it needs inside the square brackets.

blocks.title: Try one small change
blocks.text: Change the counting rule to n > 8. Work out the new answer.
